parts.text: I couldn't point to a sentence in what I read that says this, so I'm treating it as unsupported.

passages.text:
A telephone, commonly shortened to phone, is a telecommunications device that enables two or more users to conduct a conversation when they are too far apart to be easily heard directly.
A communication device for sailing vessels, called telephone, was invented by Captain John Taylor in 1844.
Alexander Graham Bell was the first to be awarded a patent for the electric telephone by the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) in March 1876.
1849: Antonio Meucci developed a voice-communication apparatus that several sources credit as the first telephone.
26 August 1854: Charles Bourseul published an article in the magazine L'Illustration (Paris): "Transmission électrique de la parole"

passages.text:
This history of the telephone chronicles the development of the electrical telephone, and includes a brief overview of its predecessors.
The first telephone patent was granted to Alexander Graham Bell in 1876.
The Elisha Gray and Alexander Bell telephone controversy considers the question of whether Bell and Gray invented the telephone independently and, if not, whether Bell stole the invention from Gray.
This controversy is narrower than the broader question of who deserves credit for inventing the telephone, for which there are several claimants.

passages.ref: nms.ac.uk — Did Alexander Graham Bell invent the telephone? | National Museums Scotland
passages.text:
Did Alexander Graham Bell invent the telephone?
Three days later, on 10 March 1876, his first intelligible telephone communication was made.
On 9 July 1877, Bell, Hubbard, Watson (and other funders) established the Bell Telephone Company to market the new device.
In 2002, the US Congress formally recognised Italian Antonio Meucci as the true inventor of the telephone.
In 1880 they formed the United Telephone Company in Britain.
